    branches: [ main ]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * 1'  # Weekly on Monday at 2 AM

# Environment configurations
env:
  NODE_VERSION: '18.x'
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}

# Workflow permissions
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  security-events: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  # Comprehensive test matrix
  test:
    name: Test Suite
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
        node-version: [16.x, 18.x, 20.x]
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            cache: npm
          - os: windows-latest
            cache: npm
          - os: macos-latest
            cache: npm
        exclude:
          - os: windows-latest
            node-version: 16.x
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
        lfs: true
    
    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        cache: ${{ matrix.cache }}
    
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        npm ci
        npm audit --audit-level high
    
    - name: Run unit tests
      run: npm run test:unit
      env:
        CI: true
        NODE_ENV: test
    
    - name: Run integration tests
      run: npm run test:integration
      env:
        TEST_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.TEST_DATABASE_URL }}
    
    - name: Upload test results
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: test-results-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.node-version }}
        path: |
          test-results/
          coverage/
        retention-days: 30
    
    - name: Publish coverage
      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
      with:
        file: ./coverage/lcov.info
        flags: unittests
        name: codecov-umbrella

  # Security scanning
  security:
    name: Security Scan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Run Snyk to check for vulnerabilities
      uses: snyk/actions/node@master
      env:
        SNYK_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SNYK_TOKEN }}
      with:
        args: --severity-threshold=high --sarif-file-output=snyk.sarif
    
    - name: Upload SARIF results
      uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
      with:
        sarif_file: snyk.sarif
    
    - name: Run CodeQL Analysis
      uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v3
      with:
        languages: javascript
        queries: security-extended

  # Build and containerize
  build:
    name: Build & Containerize
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [test, security]
    
    outputs:
      image-tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
      digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
    
    - name: Log in to Container Registry
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    
    - name: Extract metadata
      id: meta
      uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
      with:
        images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        tags: |
          type=ref,event=branch
          type=ref,event=pr
          type=semver,pattern={{version}}
          type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
          type=sha,prefix={{branch}}-
    
    - name: Build and push
      id: build
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
        tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
        labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
        cache-from: type=gha
        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

  # Deployment to environments
  deploy-staging:
    name: Deploy to Staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build
    environment: staging
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'
    
    steps:
    - name: Deploy to staging
      run: |
        echo "Deploying ${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }} to staging"
        # Add your deployment commands here
        # kubectl set image deployment/app app=${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }}
    
    - name: Run smoke tests
      run: |
        echo "Running smoke tests on staging"
        npm run test:smoke

  deploy-production:
    name: Deploy to Production
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build, deploy-staging]
    environment: production
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    
    steps:
    - name: Approve production deployment
      uses: trstringer/manual-approval@v1
      with:
        secret: ${{ github.token }}
        approvers: ${{ vars.PRODUCTION_APPROVERS }}
        minimum-approvals: 1
        issue-title: "Production Deployment Approval"
        issue-body: "Please review and approve this production deployment"
    
    - name: Deploy to production
      run: |
        echo "Deploying ${{ needs.build.outputs.image-tag }} to production"
        # Add your production deployment commands here

  # Notifications
  notify:
    name: Notify Team
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build, deploy-production]
    if: always()
    
    steps:
    - name: Notify Slack
      uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
      with:
        status: ${{ job.status }}
        channel: '#deployments'
        webhook_url: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}
      env:
        SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}

## Enterprise Git Architecture & Scale

Large organizations face unique challenges when scaling Git and GitHub across hundreds of teams and thousands of repositories. A structured approach ensures security, compliance, and developer productivity.

### Enterprise Scaling Patterns:

**Repository Strategy**
- **Monorepo**: Single repository for multiple projects/services
- **Polyrepo**: Separate repositories for each service/component
- **Hybrid**: Core monorepo with satellite repositories

**Access Control Models**
- **Centralized**: IT-managed permissions and groups
- **Federated**: Team-based ownership with oversight
- **Self-service**: Teams manage their own repositories with guardrails

**CI/CD Architecture**
- **Centralized Pipeline**: Shared CI/CD infrastructure
- **Federated Pipelines**: Team-owned with shared templates
- **Hybrid Approach**: Core platform with team customization

**Compliance & Governance**
- **Policy as Code**: Automated compliance checks
- **Audit Trail**: Comprehensive activity logging
- **Security Scanning**: Integrated vulnerability management

content.code:
#!/bin/bash

# Enterprise Git Configuration and Security Setup

# Global Git configuration for enterprise
echo "Configuring enterprise Git settings..."

# Core Git configuration
git config --global user.useconfigonly true
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global pull.rebase false

# Security settings
git config --global core.autocrlf input
git config --global core.safecrlf true
git config --global core.whitespace 'fix,-indent-with-non-tab,trailing-space,cr-at-eol'
git config --global transfer.fsckobjects true
git config --global fetch.fsckobjects true
git config --global receive.fsckObjects true

# Enterprise-specific aliases and helpers
git config --global alias.enterprise-log "log --graph --abbrev-commit --decorate --format=format:'%C(bold blue)%h%C(reset) - %C(bold green)(%ar)%C(reset) %C(white)%s%C(reset) %C(dim white)- %an%C(reset)%C(bold yellow)%d%C(reset)'"

# Pre-commit hook template for enterprise security
echo "Creating enterprise pre-commit hook template..."

cat > .githooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash

# Enterprise Security Pre-commit Hook

RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${YELLOW}🔒 Running enterprise security checks...${NC}"

# Check for secrets and credentials
PATTERNS=(
    "[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40}"  # Generic API keys
    "[0-9a-fA-F]{32}"    # MD5 hashes
    "[0-9a-fA-F]{40}"    # SHA-1 hashes
    "[0-9a-fA-F]{64}"    # SHA-256 hashes
    "xox[pborsa]-[0-9]{12}"  # Slack tokens
    "sk_live_[0-9a-zA-Z]{24}"  # Stripe keys
)

for pattern in "${PATTERNS[@]}"; do
    if git diff --cached --name-only | xargs grep -nE "$pattern" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${RED}❌ Potential secret detected with pattern: $pattern${NC}"
        echo "Please remove any secrets before committing."
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Check file sizes
MAX_SIZE=10485760  # 10MB
LARGE_FILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only | xargs -I {} find {} -type f -size +${MAX_SIZE}c 2>/dev/null)

if [ ! -z "$LARGE_FILES" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}❌ Files larger than 10MB detected:${NC}"
    echo "$LARGE_FILES"
    echo "Please use Git LFS for large files."
    exit 1
fi

# License header check
if [ -f "HEADER" ]; then
    while read -r file; do
        if [ -f "$file" ] && [[ "$file" =~ \.(js|ts|java|py)$ ]]; then
            if ! head -n 5 "$file" | grep -q "Copyright"; then
                echo -e "${RED}❌ Missing license header in: $file${NC}"
                exit 1
            fi
        fi
    done < <(git diff --cached --name-only)
fi

# Prohibited file types
PROHIBITED_EXTENSIONS=(".pem" ".key" ".crt" ".pfx" ".p12")
for ext in "${PROHIBITED_EXTENSIONS[@]}"; do
    if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q "\$ext$"; then
        echo -e "${RED}❌ Prohibited file type detected: $ext${NC}"
        echo "Please remove certificate files from version control."
        exit 1
    fi
done

echo -e "${GREEN}✅ All security checks passed!${NC}"
exit 0
EOF

chmod +x .githooks/pre-commit

# Configure enterprise Git LFS
echo "Configuring Git LFS for enterprise..."
git lfs install --skip-repo

# Common enterprise file types for LFS
git lfs track "*.psd"
git lfs track "*.ai"
git lfs track "*.zip"
git lfs track "*.tar.gz"
git lfs track "*.jar"
git lfs track "*.war"
git lfs track "*.mp4"
git lfs track "*.mov"

# Enterprise Git hook configuration
echo "Setting up enterprise Git hooks..."
git config --global core.hooksPath .githooks

# Create enterprise commit message template
cat > .gitmessage << 'EOF'
# Enterprise Commit Message Format
# 
# Format: <type>(<scope>): <subject>
# 
# Types:
#   feat:     A new feature
#   fix:      A bug fix
#   docs:     Documentation only changes
#   style:    Changes that do not affect the meaning (white-space, formatting, etc)
#   refactor: A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
#   perf:     A code change that improves performance
#   test:     Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
#   chore:    Changes to the build process or auxiliary tools
#   security: Security-related changes
# 
# Scope: The scope should be the name of the module/component affected
# 
# Subject: The subject contains a succinct description of the change
#   - Use imperative, present tense: "change" not "changed" nor "changes"
#   - Don't capitalize first letter
#   - No period (.) at the end
# 
# Body: Optional, provide more contextual information about the change
#   - Explain WHAT and WHY vs. HOW
#   - Include breaking changes if any
#   - Reference related issues/PRs
# 
# Footer: Optional, metadata about the commit
#   - Breaking changes should start with BREAKING CHANGE:
#   - Reference issues with Closes, Fixes, Relates to
# 
# Examples:
# feat(auth): implement SSO integration
# fix(api): resolve null pointer in user endpoint
# docs(readme): update deployment instructions
# 
# Remember: Commit messages are forever!
EOF

git config --global commit.template .gitmessage

echo "Enterprise Git configuration complete!"
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "1. Review and customize the pre-commit hook"
echo "2. Configure Git LFS for your specific file types"
echo "3. Train team on commit message standards"
echo "4. Set up repository templates with these configurations"

questions.question: How do we handle Git performance issues in very large repositories (10GB+)?
questions.answer:
**Large Repository Optimization Strategies:**

**Repository Structure Optimization:**
```bash
# Use sparse checkout for large monorepos
git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse <url>
git sparse-checkout set app/

# Configure Git for performance
git config --global core.preloadindex true
git config --global core.fscache true
git config --global gc.auto 256

# Use partial clone for history
git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout <url>
```

**Maintenance Operations:**
```bash
# Regular repository maintenance
git gc --aggressive
git repack -ad --depth=50 --window=250

# Clean up reflog
git reflog expire --expire=now --all
git gc --prune=now

# Use commit graphs for faster history
git commit-graph write --reachable
```

**Architectural Solutions:**
- Implement Git LFS for all binary files
- Consider repository segmentation or monorepo splitting
- Use shallow clones for CI/CD (`--depth=1`)
- Implement Git virtual filesystem (GVFS) for extremely large repos
- Use specialized Git hosting solutions that handle scale

**Monitoring:**
- Track repository size growth
- Monitor clone/fetch times
- Set up alerts for performance degradation

content.code:
#!/bin/bash

# Enterprise Pre-push Hook for Quality Assurance

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${BLUE}🚀 Running enterprise pre-push validation...${NC}"

# Get the current branch
CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD)

# Protected branches that require additional validation
PROTECTED_BRANCHES=("main" "develop" "staging" "production")

# Check if pushing to protected branch
REMOTE="${1:-origin}"
REF="${2:-$CURRENT_BRANCH}"

if [[ " ${PROTECTED_BRANCHES[@]} " =~ " ${CURRENT_BRANCH} " ]]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠️  Pushing to protected branch: $CURRENT_BRANCH${NC}"
    
    # Additional validations for protected branches
    
    # Check if there are WIP commits
    if git log --oneline -n 10 | grep -i "wip\|todo\|fixme"; then
        echo -e "${RED}❌ WIP/TODO/FIXME commits detected in history${NC}"
        echo "Please remove or fix these commits before pushing to protected branch."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Verify commit message standards
    echo -e "${BLUE}📝 Validating commit messages...${NC}"
    while read -r commit; do
        if ! echo "$commit" | grep -qE "^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|test|chore|perf|build|ci|revert)(\(.+\))?: .{1,50}"; then
            echo -e "${RED}❌ Invalid commit message format:${NC}"
            echo "  $commit"
            echo ""
            echo "Commit messages must follow: <type>(<scope>): <subject>"
            echo "Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, perf, build, ci, revert"
            exit 1
        fi
    done < <(git log --oneline --format=%s "$REMOTE/$CURRENT_BRANCH..HEAD")
    
    # Check test coverage (if available)
    if [ -f "coverage/lcov.info" ]; then
        COVERAGE=$(npx coverage-percentage coverage/lcov.info --lcov)
        MIN_COVERAGE=80
        
        if [ "${COVERAGE%.*}" -lt "$MIN_COVERAGE" ]; then
            echo -e "${RED}❌ Test coverage ${COVERAGE}% is below required ${MIN_COVERAGE}%${NC}"
            exit 1
        else
            echo -e "${GREEN}✅ Test coverage: ${COVERAGE}%${NC}"
        fi
    fi
    
    # Security scan for dependencies
    if command -v npm > /dev/null && [ -f "package.json" ]; then
        echo -e "${BLUE}🔒 Running security audit...${NC}"
        
        # Check for known vulnerabilities
        if npm audit --audit-level high; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✅ No high-severity vulnerabilities found${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "${RED}❌ High-severity vulnerabilities detected${NC}"
            echo "Run 'npm audit fix' to address these issues."
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    
    # License compliance check
    if command -v license-checker > /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${BLUE}📄 Checking license compliance...${NC}"
        
        # Generate license report
        license-checker --json --out licenses.json
        
        # Check for prohibited licenses
        PROHIBITED_LICENSES=("GPL" "AGPL" "SSPL")
        for license in "${PROHIBITED_LICENSES[@]}"; do
            if grep -q "$license" licenses.json; then
                echo -e "${RED}❌ Prohibited license detected: $license${NC}"
                rm licenses.json
                exit 1
            fi
        done
        
        rm licenses.json
        echo -e "${GREEN}✅ License compliance check passed${NC}"
    fi
    
    # Size validation for bundles (if applicable)
    if [ -f "dist" ] && command -v du > /dev/null; then
        BUNDLE_SIZE=$(du -sh dist | cut -f1)
        echo -e "${BLUE}📦 Bundle size: $BUNDLE_SIZE${NC}"
        
        # Add size limits check here if needed
    fi
    
    # Final approval for protected branch push
    echo ""
    echo -e "${GREEN}✅ All protected branch validations passed!${NC}"
    echo -e "${YELLOW}📋 Summary for $CURRENT_BRANCH:${NC}"
    echo "  ✓ Commit message standards"
    echo "  ✓ No WIP/TODO/FIXME commits"
    if [ -f "coverage/lcov.info" ]; then echo "  ✓ Test coverage requirements"; fi
    if command -v npm > /dev/null; then echo "  ✓ Security audit"; fi
    if command -v license-checker > /dev/null; then echo "  ✓ License compliance"; fi
    
else
    echo -e "${GREEN}✅ Pushing to feature branch: $CURRENT_BRANCH${NC}"
    echo "Basic validation passed. Protected branch rules do not apply."
fi

echo ""
echo -e "${GREEN}🚀 Pre-push validation complete. Pushing changes...${NC}"
exit 0

content.title: 🛒 E-commerce Testing Overview
content.content: E-commerce applications require rigorous testing across multiple dimensions - functionality, performance, security, and user experience. This course covers comprehensive testing strategies tailored for online retail platforms, integrating test management tools like TestRail and Zephyr for efficient test planning and execution.

content.title: E-commerce Application Architecture
content.explanation:
Modern e-commerce platforms typically follow a multi-tier architecture:

**Frontend Layers:**
- Web Application (React, Angular, Vue)
- Mobile Apps (iOS, Android)
- PWA (Progressive Web App)

**Backend Services:**
- Product Catalog Service
- Shopping Cart Service
- Order Management Service
- Payment Gateway Integration
- Inventory Management
- User Authentication Service
- Recommendation Engine

**Third-Party Integrations:**
- Payment Processors (Stripe, PayPal)
- Shipping Carriers (FedEx, UPS)
- Email Service Providers
- CRM Systems
- Analytics Platforms

Understanding this architecture is crucial for designing comprehensive test strategies that cover all integration points and potential failure modes.
content.analogy: Think of an e-commerce application like a modern shopping mall. The frontend is the store facade and layout that customers see. The backend services are the stock rooms, payment counters, and management offices. Third-party integrations are like external delivery services and banking partners. Testing ensures everything works harmoniously - from the moment a customer enters to when they receive their purchase.

## Test Management Tool Strategy

Effective test management is crucial for e-commerce applications due to their complexity and frequent releases. TestRail and Zephyr provide structured approaches to test planning, execution, and reporting.

### Tool Selection Criteria:

**TestRail Advantages:**
- Comprehensive test case management
- Customizable workflows and fields
- Advanced reporting and metrics
- Integration with JIRA, GitHub, and automation tools
- Milestone and release planning

**Zephyr Advantages:**
- Native JIRA integration
- Real-time test execution
- BDD support with Cucumber integration
- Scale Enterprise for large teams
- Smart Folder organization

**Common Features:**
- Test case versioning
- Requirement traceability
- Test run management
- Defect tracking integration
- Custom dashboards and reports

content.title: TestRail Test Suite Structure for E-commerce
content.code:
# E-commerce Test Suite Structure

## Project: E-commerce Platform v2.0

### 1. Smoke Test Suite
- **Priority**: Critical Paths
- **Frequency**: Daily/Pre-release
- **Scope**: Core shopping functionality

#### Test Sections:
1.1 User Authentication
  - TC001: User registration with valid data
  - TC002: Login with correct credentials
  - TC003: Login failure with invalid credentials
  - TC004: Password reset functionality

1.2 Product Catalog
  - TC010: Product search with keywords
  - TC011: Filter products by category
  - TC012: Sort products by price/rating
  - TC013: Product detail page display

1.3 Shopping Cart
  - TC020: Add product to cart
  - TC021: Update cart quantities
  - TC022: Remove items from cart
  - TC023: Cart persistence between sessions

1.4 Checkout Process
  - TC030: Guest checkout flow
  - TC031: Registered user checkout
  - TC032: Multiple payment methods
  - TC033: Order confirmation

### 2. Regression Test Suite
- **Priority**: Full Coverage
- **Frequency**: Weekly/Per release
- **Scope**: All major functionalities

#### Test Sections:
2.1 User Management
2.2 Product Management
2.3 Order Management
2.4 Payment Processing
2.5 Shipping & Tax
2.6 Promotions & Discounts
2.7 Search & Navigation
2.8 Mobile Responsiveness

### 3. Integration Test Suite
- **Priority**: API & Third-party
- **Frequency**: Per build
- **Scope**: External service integrations

#### Test Sections:
3.1 Payment Gateway APIs
3.2 Shipping Carrier APIs
3.3 Email Service Integration
3.4 Inventory Management System
3.5 CRM Integration

### 4. Performance Test Suite
- **Priority**: Load & Stress
- **Frequency**: Monthly/Major releases
- **Scope**: System performance under load

### 5. Security Test Suite
- **Priority**: Vulnerability Assessment
- **Frequency**: Quarterly/Payment changes
- **Scope**: Security compliance and data protection

## Test Case Template

**Fields for Each Test Case:**
- Title: Descriptive test case name
- Priority: High/Medium/Low
- Estimate: Time required for execution
- Preconditions: Setup requirements
- Test Steps: Detailed execution steps
- Expected Results: Clear success criteria
- Test Data: Required data inputs
- Automation: Yes/No with script reference

## Custom Fields for E-commerce
- Business Impact: High/Medium/Low
- Customer Journey: Browse/Cart/Checkout/Post-purchase
- Platform: Web/Mobile/API
- Payment Method: Credit Card/PayPal/Other
- User Type: Guest/Registered/Admin

questions.answer:
**Inventory Synchronization Testing:**

**Test Architecture:**
```
E-commerce Platform ↔ Inventory Management System
         ↓                    ↓
   Shopping Cart          Stock Levels
         ↓                    ↓
     Order System        Inventory Updates
```

**Critical Test Scenarios:**
1. **Real-time stock updates**
   - Add to cart reduces available quantity
   - Abandoned cart restores inventory
   - Concurrent purchases prevent overselling

2. **Batch synchronization**
   - Scheduled inventory imports/exports
   - Bulk product updates
   - Price and attribute synchronization

3. **Error handling**
   - Inventory system downtime
   - Data format mismatches
   - Network connectivity issues

**Testing Tools & Techniques:**
```sql
-- Database queries to verify synchronization
SELECT product_id, web_stock, warehouse_stock, difference
FROM inventory_sync_view
WHERE difference != 0;

-- API testing for inventory updates
POST /api/inventory/update
{
  "product_id": "123",
  "quantity": -1,
  "source": "order_placement"
}
```

**Automation Strategy:**
- Monitor inventory tables for consistency
- Simulate high-concurrency purchase scenarios
- Validate webhook responses for inventory updates
- Test with various inventory threshold levels

content.title: Test Progress Dashboard & Reporting
content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
E-commerce Test Metrics Dashboard
Generates comprehensive test execution reports and metrics
"""

import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, List, Any

class EcommerceTestMetrics:
    def __init__(self, testrail_client, jira_client):
        self.testrail = testrail_client
        self.jira = jira_client
        
    def get_test_execution_summary(self, project_id: str, days: int = 7) -> Dict:
        """Generate test execution summary for the specified period"""
        
        end_date = datetime.now()
        start_date = end_date - timedelta(days=days)
        
        # Get test runs and results
        test_runs = self.testrail.get_runs(project_id, created_after=start_date)
        
        summary = {
            "period": f"{start_date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')} to {end_date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}",
            "total_test_runs": len(test_runs),
            "test_cases_executed": 0,
            "test_cases_passed": 0,
            "test_cases_failed": 0,
            "test_cases_blocked": 0,
            "defects_found": 0,
            "defects_fixed": 0,
            "defects_open": 0,
            "coverage_metrics": {},
            "risk_areas": []
        }
        
        for test_run in test_runs:
            results = self.testrail.get_results(test_run['id'])
            
            for result in results:
                summary["test_cases_executed"] += 1
                
                if result['status_id'] == 1:  # Passed
                    summary["test_cases_passed"] += 1
                elif result['status_id'] == 5:  # Failed
                    summary["test_cases_failed"] += 1
                    summary["defects_found"] += 1
                elif result['status_id'] == 2:  # Blocked
                    summary["test_cases_blocked"] += 1
        
        # Calculate additional metrics
        summary["pass_rate"] = (summary["test_cases_passed"] / summary["test_cases_executed"]) * 100
        summary["test_efficiency"] = summary["test_cases_executed"] / len(test_runs)
        
        # Get defect metrics from JIRA
        defect_metrics = self.get_defect_metrics(start_date, end_date)
        summary.update(defect_metrics)
        
        # Calculate coverage metrics
        summary["coverage_metrics"] = self.calculate_coverage_metrics(project_id)
        
        # Identify risk areas
        summary["risk_areas"] = self.identify_risk_areas(summary)
        
        return summary
    
    def calculate_coverage_metrics(self, project_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Calculate test coverage across different e-commerce components"""
        
        coverage = {
            "user_management": 0,
            "product_catalog": 0,
            "shopping_cart": 0,
            "checkout_process": 0,
            "payment_processing": 0,
            "order_management": 0,
            "mobile_experience": 0,
            "api_integrations": 0
        }
        
        # Get all test cases and categorize by component
        test_cases = self.testrail.get_cases(project_id)
        
        component_count = {key: 0 for key in coverage.keys()}
        
        for test_case in test_cases:
            # Categorize based on section or custom fields
            component = self.categorize_test_case(test_case)
            if component in component_count:
                component_count[component] += 1
        
        total_cases = len(test_cases)
        
        for component, count in component_count.items():
            if total_cases > 0:
                coverage[component] = (count / total_cases) * 100
        
        return coverage
    
    def categorize_test_case(self, test_case: Dict) -> str:
        """Categorize test case into e-commerce components"""
        
        # Implementation depends on your TestRail structure
        # This is a simplified example
        title = test_case.get('title', '').lower()
        
        if any(word in title for word in ['login', 'register', 'profile', 'password']):
            return "user_management"
        elif any(word in title for word in ['product', 'catalog', 'search', 'filter']):
            return "product_catalog"
        elif any(word in title for word in ['cart', 'basket', 'add to cart']):
            return "shopping_cart"
        elif any(word in title for word in ['checkout', 'payment', 'pay', 'credit card']):
            return "checkout_process"
        elif any(word in title for word in ['order', 'confirmation', 'tracking']):
            return "order_management"
        elif any(word in title for word in ['mobile', 'responsive', 'app']):
            return "mobile_experience"
        elif any(word in title for word in ['api', 'integration', 'webhook']):
            return "api_integrations"
        else:
            return "checkout_process"  # Default
    
    def get_defect_metrics(self, start_date: datetime, end_date: datetime) -> Dict:
        """Get defect-related metrics from JIRA"""
        
        # JQL query for defects in the date range
        jql = f'project = "ECOMM" AND created >= "{start_date.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")}" AND created <= "{end_date.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%d\")}"'
        
        issues = self.jira.search_issues(jql)
        
        defect_metrics = {
            "defects_found": len(issues),
            "defects_fixed": 0,
            "defects_open": 0,
            "defects_critical": 0,
            "defects_by_component": {},
            "defect_trend": "stable"
        }
        
        for issue in issues:
            status = issue.fields.status.name
            
            if status in ['Done', 'Closed', 'Resolved']:
                defect_metrics["defects_fixed"] += 1
            else:
                defect_metrics["defects_open"] += 1
            
            # Count critical defects
            if issue.fields.priority.name == 'Critical':
                defect_metrics["defects_critical"] += 1
            
            # Categorize by component
            component = getattr(issue.fields, 'components', [None])[0] if getattr(issue.fields, 'components', []) else 'Unknown'
            if component:
                component_name = component.name
                defect_metrics["defects_by_component"][component_name] = defect_metrics["defects_by_component"].get(component_name, 0) + 1
        
        return defect_metrics
    
    def identify_risk_areas(self, summary: Dict) -> List[str]:
        """Identify potential risk areas based on metrics"""
        
        risks = []
        
        # Check pass rate
        if summary["pass_rate"] < 80:
            risks.append(f"Low pass rate: {summary['pass_rate']:.1f}% - indicates potential quality issues")
        
        # Check critical defects
        if summary["defects_critical"] > 5:
            risks.append(f"High number of critical defects: {summary['defects_critical']} - requires immediate attention")
        
        # Check component coverage
        for component, coverage in summary["coverage_metrics"].items():
            if coverage < 60:
                risks.append(f"Low test coverage for {component}: {coverage:.1f}% - consider adding more test cases")
        
        # Check defect fix rate
        if summary["defects_fixed"] / max(summary["defects_found"], 1) < 0.7:
            risks.append("Low defect fix rate - may impact release timeline")
        
        return risks
    
    def generate_execution_report(self, project_id: str) -> str:
        """Generate formatted execution report"""
        
        summary = self.get_test_execution_summary(project_id)
        
        report = f"""
E-COMMERCE TEST EXECUTION REPORT
================================
Period: {summary['period']}

EXECUTION SUMMARY:
-----------------
Total Test Runs: {summary['total_test_runs']}
Test Cases Executed: {summary['test_cases_executed']}
Test Cases Passed: {summary['test_cases_passed']}
Test Cases Failed: {summary['test_cases_failed']}
Test Cases Blocked: {summary['test_cases_blocked']}
Pass Rate: {summary['pass_rate']:.1f}%

DEFECT METRICS:
--------------
Defects Found: {summary['defects_found']}
Defects Fixed: {summary['defects_fixed']}
Defects Open: {summary['defects_open']}
Critical Defects: {summary['defects_critical']}

TEST COVERAGE:
-------------
"""
        
        for component, coverage in summary["coverage_metrics"].items():
            report += f"{component.replace('_', ' ').title()}: {coverage:.1f}%\n"
        
        if summary["risk_areas"]:
            report += "\nRISK AREAS:\n-----------\n"
            for risk in summary["risk_areas"]:
                report += f"• {risk}\n"
        
        return report

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Initialize with your TestRail and JIRA clients
    metrics = EcommerceTestMetrics(testrail_client, jira_client)
    report = metrics.generate_execution_report("ecommerce-project")
    print(report)
content.caption: Python script for generating comprehensive e-commerce test execution metrics and reports, integrating with TestRail and JIRA for data collection.

```json
  "user_journeys": [
    {
      "name": "Product Browsing",

    },
    {
      "name": "Checkout Process",
      "percentage": 20,
      "actions": ["checkout_start", "shipping_selection", "payment_processing"]
    },
    {
      "name": "High-Value Purchases",
      "percentage": 10,
      "actions": ["premium_products", "multiple_quantities", "express_checkout"]
    }
  ]

```

**Critical System Components to Test:**
- **Product Catalog**: Search performance, filter responsiveness
- **Inventory System**: Stock reservation, oversell prevention
- **Shopping Cart**: Concurrent updates, cart abandonment
- **Payment Gateway**: Transaction throughput, error handling
- **Order Processing**: Order creation, confirmation emails

**Performance Benchmarks:**
- Page load times < 3 seconds
- Search results < 2 seconds
- Add to cart < 1 second

content.title: 📊 Module 1: Financial Domain Fundamentals & Regulatory Landscape
Banking System Architecture & Components
content.explanation:
Modern banking systems comprise multiple interconnected components that must work in harmony while maintaining strict security and compliance standards.

**Core Banking Components:**
- **Core Banking System (CBS)**: Central processing for accounts, loans, transactions

- Credit/debit card processors
- Credit rating agencies

- Third-party financial services

**Data Flow Complexity:**

```sql
('Recurring Deposit', 5000.00, 5.500, 'monthly', 'quarterly', 68.75, '2024-03-31');
```

**Calculation Validation Approach:**

**Daily Interest Calculation:**
```python
def validate_daily_interest_calculation(principal, annual_rate, days, expected_interest):
    """Validate daily interest calculation with rounding rules"""
    
    daily_rate = annual_rate / 36500  # Convert to decimal and adjust for days
    calculated_interest = principal * daily_rate * days
    
    # Apply banking rounding rules (usually to 2 decimal places)
    calculated_interest = round(calculated_interest, 2)
    
    assert abs(calculated_interest - expected_interest) < 0.01, \
        f"Interest calculation mismatch: {calculated_interest} vs {expected_interest}"
    
    return True
```

**Critical Test Scenarios:**
- **Leap year calculations**: 366 vs 365 days
- **Different day count conventions**: Actual/365, 30/360, Actual/360
- **Compounding frequencies**: Daily, monthly, quarterly, yearly
- **Partial period calculations**: Account opening/closing mid-period
- **Minimum balance penalties**: Impact on interest eligibility
- **Tax deduction at source**: Net vs gross interest amounts

- APR (Annual Percentage Rate) accuracy
- Truth in Lending Act compliance
- Local regulatory interest calculation rules
- Disclosure requirements validation

content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Banking Test Metrics Dashboard
Comprehensive reporting for banking application testing with regulatory focus
"""

import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, List, Any
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class RegulatoryRequirement:
    regulation: str
    requirement_id: str
    description: str
    test_coverage: float
    compliance_status: str
    last_audit_date: datetime

class BankingTestMetrics:
    def __init__(self, testrail_client, jira_client, compliance_db):
        self.testrail = testrail_client
        self.jira = jira_client
        self.compliance_db = compliance_db
    
    def get_regulatory_compliance_report(self, project_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Generate comprehensive regulatory compliance report"""
        
        # Get regulatory requirements from compliance database
        regulatory_reqs = self.compliance_db.get_regulatory_requirements()
        
        # Get test cases mapped to regulatory requirements
        test_cases = self.testrail.get_cases(project_id)
        
        compliance_report = {
            "report_date": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "regulatory_requirements": [],
            "overall_compliance_score": 0,
            "high_risk_areas": [],
            "audit_readiness": "",
            "recommendations": []
        }
        
        total_requirements = len(regulatory_reqs)
        compliant_requirements = 0
        
        for req in regulatory_reqs:
            # Find test cases mapped to this requirement
            mapped_cases = [tc for tc in test_cases if self.is_case_mapped_to_requirement(tc, req)]
            
            if mapped_cases:
                # Calculate test coverage for this requirement
                coverage = self.calculate_requirement_coverage(mapped_cases)
                status = self.determine_compliance_status(coverage, mapped_cases)
                
                if status == "Compliant":
                    compliant_requirements += 1
                
                requirement_report = {
                    "regulation": req.regulation,
                    "requirement_id": req.requirement_id,
                    "description": req.description,
                    "test_coverage": coverage,
                    "compliance_status": status,
                    "mapped_test_cases": len(mapped_cases),
                    "last_tested": self.get_last_test_date(mapped_cases),
                    "evidence_available": self.check_evidence_availability(mapped_cases)
                }
                
                compliance_report["regulatory_requirements"].append(requirement_report)
                
                # Identify high-risk areas
                if coverage < 80 or status == "Non-Compliant":
                    compliance_report["high_risk_areas"].append({
                        "requirement": req.requirement_id,
                        "risk": "Insufficient test coverage" if coverage < 80 else "Non-compliant",
                        "impact": "Regulatory penalty risk"
                    })
        
        # Calculate overall compliance score
        if total_requirements > 0:
            compliance_report["overall_compliance_score"] = (compliant_requirements / total_requirements) * 100
        
        # Determine audit readiness
        compliance_report["audit_readiness"] = self.assess_audit_readiness(compliance_report)
        
        # Generate recommendations
        compliance_report["recommendations"] = self.generate_compliance_recommendations(compliance_report)
        
        return compliance_report
    
    def get_financial_accuracy_report(self, project_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Report on financial calculation accuracy testing"""
        
        financial_modules = [
            "interest_calculation",
            "loan_processing", 
            "tax_calculation",
            "forex_processing",
            "commission_calculation"
        ]
        
        accuracy_report = {
            "financial_modules": {},
            "calculation_errors": [],
            "data_integrity_issues": [],
            "reconciliation_gaps": []
        }
        
        for module in financial_modules:
            module_cases = self.testrail.get_cases(project_id, section=module)
            
            if module_cases:
                execution_results = self.get_module_execution_results(module_cases)
                
                accuracy_report["financial_modules"][module] = {
                    "total_cases": len(module_cases),
                    "executed_cases": execution_results["executed"],
                    "passed_cases": execution_results["passed"],
                    "calculation_errors": execution_results["calculation_errors"],
                    "accuracy_rate": (execution_results["passed"] / execution_results["executed"]) * 100 if execution_results["executed"] > 0 else 0
                }
                
                # Track calculation errors
                if execution_results["calculation_errors"] > 0:
                    accuracy_report["calculation_errors"].append({
                        "module": module,
                        "error_count": execution_results["calculation_errors"],
                        "severity": "High" if module in ["interest_calculation", "tax_calculation"] else "Medium"
                    })
        
        return accuracy_report
    
    def get_risk_assessment_report(self, project_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Generate risk-based testing assessment report"""
        
        risk_categories = {
            "high": {
                "weight": 0.6,
                "test_cases": [],
                "pass_rate": 0
            },
            "medium": {
                "weight": 0.3, 
                "test_cases": [],
                "pass_rate": 0
            },
            "low": {
                "weight": 0.1,
                "test_cases": [],
                "pass_rate": 0
            }
        }
        
        # Categorize test cases by risk
        test_cases = self.testrail.get_cases(project_id)
        
        for test_case in test_cases:
            risk_level = self.assess_test_case_risk(test_case)
            risk_categories[risk_level]["test_cases"].append(test_case)
        
        # Calculate pass rates for each risk category
        for risk_level in risk_categories:
            cases = risk_categories[risk_level]["test_cases"]
            if cases:
                executed_cases = [c for c in cases if self.is_case_executed(c)]
                passed_cases = [c for c in executed_cases if self.is_case_passed(c)]
                
                if executed_cases:
                    risk_categories[risk_level]["pass_rate"] = (len(passed_cases) / len(executed_cases)) * 100
        
        # Calculate overall risk score
        overall_risk_score = sum(
            risk_categories[level]["weight"] * (100 - risk_categories[level]["pass_rate"])
            for level in risk_categories
        )
        
        risk_report = {
            "risk_assessment_date": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "risk_categories": risk_categories,
            "overall_risk_score": overall_risk_score,
            "risk_level": self.determine_risk_level(overall_risk_score),
            "mitigation_recommendations": self.generate_risk_mitigation_recommendations(risk_categories)
        }
        
        return risk_report
    
    def generate_executive_summary(self, project_id: str) -> str:
        """Generate executive summary for banking stakeholders"""
        
        compliance_report = self.get_regulatory_compliance_report(project_id)
        accuracy_report = self.get_financial_accuracy_report(project_id)
        risk_report = self.get_risk_assessment_report(project_id)
        
        summary = f"""
BANKING APPLICATION TESTING EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
============================================
Report Date: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}

REGULATORY COMPLIANCE STATUS:
-----------------------------
Overall Compliance Score: {compliance_report['overall_compliance_score']:.1f}%
Audit Readiness: {compliance_report['audit_readiness']}
High-Risk Areas: {len(compliance_report['high_risk_areas'])}

FINANCIAL ACCURACY ASSESSMENT:
-----------------------------
"""
        
        for module, metrics in accuracy_report["financial_modules"].items():
            summary += f"{module.replace('_', ' ').title()}: {metrics['accuracy_rate']:.1f}% accuracy\n"
        
        summary += f"""
RISK ASSESSMENT:
---------------
Overall Risk Score: {risk_report['overall_risk_score']:.1f}/100
Risk Level: {risk_report['risk_level']}

CRITICAL FINDINGS:
-----------------
"""
        
        # Add critical findings from all reports
        if compliance_report["high_risk_areas"]:
            summary += "Regulatory Compliance Issues:\n"
            for risk in compliance_report["high_risk_areas"][:3]:  # Top 3
                summary += f"• {risk['requirement']}: {risk['risk']}\n"
        
        if accuracy_report["calculation_errors"]:
            summary += "\nFinancial Calculation Errors:\n"
            for error in accuracy_report["calculation_errors"][:3]:  # Top 3
                summary += f"• {error['module']}: {error['error_count']} errors ({error['severity']} severity)\n"
        
        summary += "\nRECOMMENDATIONS:\n---------------\n"
        for rec in compliance_report["recommendations"][:5]:  # Top 5
            summary += f"• {rec}\n"
        
        return summary

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":

**AI/ML Model Testing Strategy for Banking:**

**Model Validation Framework:**

**Data Quality Testing:**
```python
class ModelDataValidator:
    def validate_training_data(self, dataset):
        """Comprehensive training data validation"""
        
        checks = {
            'completeness': self.check_data_completeness(dataset),
            'accuracy': self.validate_data_accuracy(dataset),
            'consistency': self.check_temporal_consistency(dataset),
            'bias_detection': self.detect_data_bias(dataset),
            'regulatory_compliance': self.check_regulatory_constraints(dataset)
        }
        
        return all(checks.values()), checks
    
    def detect_data_bias(self, dataset):
        """Check for demographic or geographic bias in training data"""
        
        # Implement fairness testing algorithms
        demographic_columns = ['age', 'gender', 'location', 'income_bracket']
        
        for column in demographic_columns:
            if column in dataset.columns:
                distribution = dataset[column].value_counts(normalize=True)
                # Check if distribution matches expected population distribution
                if not self.validate_fair_distribution(distribution):
                    return False
        
        return True
```

**Model Performance Testing:**
- **Accuracy Metrics**: Precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC
- **Business Impact Validation**: False positive/negative cost analysis
- **Stability Testing**: Model performance over time and data drift
- **Explainability Testing**: Ability to explain model decisions to regulators

**Regulatory Compliance Testing:**
```python
class ModelComplianceValidator:
    def validate_model_compliance(self, model, regulations):
        """Validate model against banking regulations"""
        
        compliance_checks = {
            'fair_lending': self.check_fair_lending_compliance(model),
            'model_risk_management': self.validate_model_risk_framework(model),
            'explainability': self.test_model_explainability(model),
            'documentation': self.verify_model_documentation(model),
            'governance': self.check_model_governance_processes(model)
        }
        
        return compliance_checks
    
    def check_fair_lending_compliance(self, model):
        """Ensure model doesn't create discriminatory outcomes"""
        
        # Test for disparate impact
        protected_classes = ['race', 'gender', 'age', 'ethnicity']
        
        for protected_class in protected_classes:
            disparity_ratio = self.calculate_disparate_impact(model, protected_class)
            if disparity_ratio < 0.8 or disparity_ratio > 1.25:
                return False  # Potential discrimination detected
        
        return True
```

**Model Monitoring & Drift Detection:**
- **Concept Drift**: Model performance degradation over time
- **Data Drift**: Changes in input data distribution
- **Bias Drift**: Evolving fairness characteristics
- **Alert Thresholds**: Automated alerts for model degradation

**Back-testing & Scenario Analysis:**

content.title: ⚕️ Module 1: Healthcare Domain Fundamentals & Regulatory Landscape
Healthcare System Architecture & Components
content.explanation:
Modern healthcare systems comprise complex interconnected components that must maintain strict data integrity, security, and clinical accuracy while supporting life-critical operations.

**Core Healthcare Components:**
- **Electronic Health Record (EHR) Systems**: Comprehensive patient health information
- **Practice Management Systems**: Scheduling, billing, and administrative functions
- **Clinical Decision Support Systems**: Evidence-based clinical recommendations
- **Medical Imaging Systems**: PACS, RIS for diagnostic imaging
- **Laboratory Information Systems**: Test orders and results management
- **Pharmacy Management Systems**: Medication ordering and dispensing
- **Telemedicine Platforms**: Remote patient consultations

**Integration Points:**
- HL7/FHIR interfaces for healthcare data exchange
- Medical device integrations (monitors, pumps, scanners)
- Insurance claim processing systems
- Pharmacy benefit managers
- Public health reporting systems
- Laboratory and diagnostic centers

**Data Standards & Protocols:**
- HL7 v2/v3 for clinical data exchange
- FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources)
- DICOM for medical imaging
- ICD-10/CPT codes for diagnoses and procedures
- SNOMED CT for clinical terminology
- LOINC for laboratory observations
content.analogy: Think of a healthcare system like a modern hospital. The EHR is the central patient chart containing all medical history. Clinical systems are the specialized departments (radiology, lab, pharmacy). Integration points are the communication channels between departments. Regulatory requirements are the medical standards and protocols that ensure patient safety. Testing ensures all these components work together seamlessly while maintaining the highest standards of care and data protection.

content.title: Healthcare Test Scenarios - Gherkin Format
content.code:
Feature: Electronic Health Record Clinical Workflows

  Background:
    Given the EHR system is operational
    And test patient records are available
    And clinical users are authenticated with appropriate roles

  Scenario: Physician completes medication order with safety checks
    Given a patient with documented penicillin allergy
    When physician orders Amoxicillin 500mg PO TID
    Then system should display critical drug-allergy interaction alert
    And physician should be required to acknowledge the alert
    When physician overrides the alert with reason "Patient tolerance confirmed"
    Then medication order should be processed
    And override reason should be documented in audit trail
    And pharmacy should receive order with allergy alert notation

  Scenario: Nurse administers high-risk medication with double verification
    Given a patient with Heparin infusion order
    And infusion pump is connected to EHR
    When nurse scans patient wristband and medication barcode
    Then system should validate correct patient and medication
    And require second nurse verification for high-risk medication
    When second nurse provides verification
    Then infusion parameters should be sent to pump
    And administration should be documented in medication record
    And vital signs should be monitored for adverse reactions

  Scenario: Critical lab result notification and acknowledgment
    Given a patient with potassium level of 2.8 mEq/L (critical low)
    When lab system sends critical result to EHR
    Then system should generate urgent alert to responsible physician
    And alert should be escalated if not acknowledged within 15 minutes
    When physician acknowledges the critical result
    Then appropriate actions should be documented
    And follow-up orders should be placed if needed
    And alert should be marked as resolved

  Scenario: Patient identification and record matching
    Given multiple patients with similar demographics
    When user searches for "John Smith"
    Then system should display potential matches with distinguishing information
    And require additional verification for selection
    When user selects correct patient with confidence factors
    Then patient context should be established for all subsequent actions
    And audit trail should record the patient selection process

  Scenario: Emergency break-glass access to patient record
    Given a patient arriving in emergency situation
    And treating clinician does not have routine access to patient record
    When clinician activates emergency break-glass access
    Then system should grant temporary access to critical patient information
    And require reason for break-glass access
    And log all accessed information in security audit
    And notify security officer of the emergency access
    When emergency situation is resolved
    Then access should be automatically revoked after timeout period

  Scenario: Clinical decision support for sepsis screening
    Given a patient with elevated temperature and heart rate
    When nurse documents vital signs in EHR
    Then system should calculate NEWS2 (National Early Warning Score)
    And trigger sepsis screening protocol for elevated score
    When physician reviews sepsis screening alert
    Then system should provide evidence-based sepsis bundle recommendations
    And facilitate rapid order entry for sepsis protocol
    And track compliance with sepsis management guidelines

  Scenario: Medication reconciliation during care transitions
    Given a patient transitioning from hospital to home care
    When discharge process is initiated
    Then system should compare pre-admission medications with current orders
    And identify discrepancies and potential interactions
    And generate patient-friendly medication instructions
    And facilitate prescription transmission to pharmacy
    And document patient education provided

  Scenario: Telemedicine consultation with remote monitoring
    Given a patient with chronic condition on remote monitoring
    When patient's vital signs exceed predefined thresholds
    Then system should alert care team for intervention
    When video consultation is initiated
    Then system should integrate remote monitoring data with video platform
    And facilitate e-prescription if needed
    And document the virtual encounter appropriately
    And update care plan based on consultation

  Scenario: Public health reporting for communicable disease
    Given a patient with confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis
    When case meets public health reporting criteria
    Then system should generate standardized report for health department
    And transmit report via secure public health interface
    And confirm successful submission

```python
class MedicationSafetyValidator:
    def validate_pediatric_dose(self, medication, patient_weight_kg, calculated_dose, route):
        """Validate pediatric medication dosage calculations"""
        
        # Get medication-specific dosing guidelines
        dosing_guidelines = self.get_dosing_guidelines(medication, 'pediatric')
        
        expected_dose = patient_weight_kg * dosing_guidelines['mg_per_kg']
        max_dose = dosing_guidelines['max_dose_mg']
        
        # Validate calculation accuracy
        assert abs(calculated_dose - expected_dose) < 0.1, \
            f"Dose calculation error: {calculated_dose} vs {expected_dose}"
        
        # Validate against maximum safe dose
        assert calculated_dose <= max_dose, \
            f"Dose exceeds maximum safe dose: {calculated_dose} > {max_dose}"
        
        # Check rounding rules (typically to nearest 0.5mg for liquids)
        if route == 'oral' and dosing_guidelines['liquid']:
            assert calculated_dose % 0.5 == 0, "Liquid dose should be rounded to nearest 0.5mg"
        
        return True
    
    def check_drug_interactions(self, medication_list, patient_allergies, existing_conditions):
        """Comprehensive drug interaction and allergy checking"""
        
        interactions = []
        
        # Check drug-allergy interactions
        for medication in medication_list:
            if self.has_allergy_conflict(medication, patient_allergies):
                interactions.append({
                    'type': 'allergy',
                    'severity': 'critical',
                    'medications': [medication],
                    'description': f'Patient has documented allergy to {medication}'
                })
        
        # Check drug-drug interactions
        for i, med1 in enumerate(medication_list):
            for med2 in medication_list[i+1:]:
                interaction = self.check_drug_drug_interaction(med1, med2)
                if interaction:
                    interactions.append(interaction)
        
        # Check drug-condition interactions
        for medication in medication_list:
            condition_interaction = self.check_drug_condition_interaction(medication, existing_conditions)
            if condition_interaction:
                interactions.append(condition_interaction)
        
        return interactions
```

content.code:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Healthcare Test Metrics Dashboard
Comprehensive reporting for healthcare application testing with patient safety focus
"""

import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Dict, List, Any
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class PatientSafetyRequirement:
    safety_protocol: str
    requirement_id: str
    description: str
    test_coverage: float
    safety_status: str
    clinical_validation: bool

class HealthcareTestMetrics:
    def __init__(self, testrail_client, jira_client, clinical_db):
        self.testrail = testrail_client
        self.jira = jira_client
        self.clinical_db = clinical_db
    
    def get_patient_safety_report(self, project_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Generate comprehensive patient safety assessment report"""
        
        # Get patient safety requirements from clinical database
        safety_requirements = self.clinical_db.get_safety_requirements()
        
        # Get test cases mapped to safety requirements
        test_cases = self.testrail.get_cases(project_id)
        
        safety_report = {
            "report_date": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "safety_requirements": [],
            "overall_safety_score": 0,
            "high_risk_findings": [],
            "clinical_validation_status": "",
            "safety_recommendations": []
        }
        
        total_requirements = len(safety_requirements)
        validated_requirements = 0
        
        for req in safety_requirements:
            # Find test cases mapped to this safety requirement
            mapped_cases = [tc for tc in test_cases if self.is_case_mapped_to_safety(tc, req)]
            
            if mapped_cases:
                # Calculate test coverage for this requirement
                coverage = self.calculate_safety_coverage(mapped_cases)
                status = self.determine_safety_status(coverage, mapped_cases, req.clinical_validation)
                
                if status == "Validated":
                    validated_requirements += 1
                
                requirement_report = {
                    "safety_protocol": req.safety_protocol,
                    "requirement_id": req.requirement_id,
                    "description": req.description,
                    "test_coverage": coverage,
                    "safety_status": status,
                    "mapped_test_cases": len(mapped_cases),
                    "clinical_validation": req.clinical_validation,
                    "last_tested": self.get_last_safety_test_date(mapped_cases),
                    "evidence_available": self.check_safety_evidence(mapped_cases)
                }
                
                safety_report["safety_requirements"].append(requirement_report)
                
                # Identify high-risk findings
                if coverage < 90 or status == "At Risk":
                    safety_report["high_risk_findings"].append({
                        "requirement": req.requirement_id,
                        "risk": "Insufficient test coverage" if coverage < 90 else "Safety validation gap",
                        "patient_impact": "Potential medication error" if "medication" in req.safety_protocol.lower() else "Clinical workflow risk"
                    })
        
        # Calculate overall safety score
        if total_requirements > 0:
            safety_report["overall_safety_score"] = (validated_requirements / total_requirements) * 100
        
        # Determine clinical validation status
        safety_report["clinical_validation_status"] = self.assess_clinical_validation(safety_report)
        
        # Generate safety recommendations
        safety_report["safety_recommendations"] = self.generate_safety_recommendations(safety_report)
        
        return safety_report
    
    def get_medication_safety_report(self, project_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Report on medication safety testing"""
        
        medication_modules = [
            "medication_ordering",
            "drug_interaction_checking", 
            "dosage_calculation",
            "medication_administration",
            "high_risk_medications"
        ]
        
        medication_report = {
            "medication_modules": {},
            "safety_incidents": [],
            "calculation_errors": [],
            "interaction_misses": []
        }
        
        for module in medication_modules:
            module_cases = self.testrail.get_cases(project_id, section=module)
            
            if module_cases:
                safety_results = self.get_medication_safety_results(module_cases)
                
                medication_report["medication_modules"][module] = {
                    "total_cases": len(module_cases),
                    "executed_cases": safety_results["executed"],
                    "passed_cases": safety_results["passed"],
                    "safety_incidents": safety_results["safety_incidents"],
                    "safety_score": (safety_results["passed"] / safety_results["executed"]) * 100 if safety_results["executed"] > 0 else 0
                }
                
                # Track safety incidents
                if safety_results["safety_incidents"] > 0:
                    medication_report["safety_incidents"].append({
                        "module": module,
                        "incident_count": safety_results["safety_incidents"],
                        "severity": "Critical" if module in ["dosage_calculation", "high_risk_medications"] else "High"
                    })
        
        return medication_report
    
    def get_hipaa_compliance_report(self, project_id: str) -> Dict:
        """Generate HIPAA compliance assessment report"""
        
        hipaa_requirements = {
            "access_controls": {
                "weight": 0.25,
                "test_cases": [],
                "compliance_status": ""
            },
            "audit_trails": {
                "weight": 0.25,
                "test_cases": [],
                "compliance_status": ""
            },
            "data_encryption": {
                "weight": 0.20,
                "test_cases": [],
                "compliance_status": ""
            },
            "phi_protection": {
                "weight": 0.30,
                "test_cases": [],
                "compliance_status": ""
            }
        }
        
        # Categorize test cases by HIPAA requirement
        test_cases = self.testrail.get_cases(project_id)
        
        for test_case in test_cases:
            hipaa_category = self.categorize_hipaa_requirement(test_case)
            if hipaa_category in hipaa_requirements:
                hipaa_requirements[hipaa_category]["test_cases"].append(test_case)
        
        # Calculate compliance status for each requirement
        for category in hipaa_requirements:
            cases = hipaa_requirements[category]["test_cases"]
            if cases:
                executed_cases = [c for c in cases if self.is_case_executed(c)]
                passed_cases = [c for c in executed_cases if self.is_case_passed(c)]
                
                if executed_cases:
                    pass_rate = (len(passed_cases) / len(executed_cases)) * 100
                    hipaa_requirements[category]["compliance_status"] = \
                        "Compliant" if pass_rate >= 95 else "Needs Improvement"
        
        # Calculate overall HIPAA compliance score
        overall_score = sum(
            hipaa_requirements[category]["weight"] * 
            (100 if hipaa_requirements[category]["compliance_status"] == "Compliant" else 50)
            for category in hipaa_requirements
        )
        
        compliance_report = {
            "assessment_date": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "hipaa_requirements": hipaa_requirements,
            "overall_compliance_score": overall_score,
            "compliance_level": self.determine_compliance_level(overall_score),
            "remediation_requirements": self.generate_hipaa_remediation(hipaa_requirements)
        }
        
        return compliance_report
    
    def generate_clinical_summary(self, project_id: str) -> str:
        """Generate clinical executive summary for healthcare stakeholders"""
        
        safety_report = self.get_patient_safety_report(project_id)
        medication_report = self.get_medication_safety_report(project_id)
        hipaa_report = self.get_hipaa_compliance_report(project_id)
        
        summary = f"""
HEALTHCARE APPLICATION TESTING EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
===============================================
Report Date: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}

PATIENT SAFETY ASSESSMENT:
-------------------------
Overall Safety Score: {safety_report['overall_safety_score']:.1f}%
Clinical Validation Status: {safety_report['clinical_validation_status']}
High-Risk Findings: {len(safety_report['high_risk_areas'])}

MEDICATION SAFETY STATUS:
------------------------
"""
        
        for module, metrics in medication_report["medication_modules"].items():
            summary += f"{module.replace('_', ' ').title()}: {metrics['safety_score']:.1f}% safety score\n"
        
        summary += f"""
HIPAA COMPLIANCE STATUS:
-----------------------
Overall Compliance Score: {hipaa_report['overall_compliance_score']:.1f}%
Compliance Level: {hipaa_report['compliance_level']}

CRITICAL CLINICAL FINDINGS:
--------------------------
"""
        
        # Add critical findings from all reports
        if safety_report["high_risk_findings"]:
            summary += "Patient Safety Concerns:\n"
            for risk in safety_report["high_risk_findings"][:3]:  # Top 3
                summary += f"• {risk['requirement']}: {risk['risk']} - {risk['patient_impact']}\n"
        
        if medication_report["safety_incidents"]:
            summary += "\nMedication Safety Issues:\n"
            for incident in medication_report["safety_incidents"][:3]:  # Top 3
                summary += f"• {incident['module']}: {incident['incident_count']} incidents ({incident['severity']} severity)\n"
        
        summary += "\nCLINICAL RECOMMENDATIONS:\n-----------------------\n"
        for rec in safety_report["safety_recommendations"][:5]:  # Top 5
            summary += f"• {rec}\n"
        
        return summary

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    metrics = HealthcareTestMetrics(testrail_client, jira_client, clinical_db)
    summary = metrics.generate_clinical_summary("ehr-system-project")
    print(summary)

```python
class MedicalDeviceValidator:
    def validate_vital_signs_integration(self, device_data, ehr_data):
        """Validate accuracy of vital signs data from medical devices"""
        
        validation_results = {
            'heart_rate': self.compare_values(device_data.heart_rate, ehr_data.heart_rate),
            'blood_pressure': self.compare_bp(device_data.bp, ehr_data.bp),
            'oxygen_saturation': self.compare_values(device_data.spo2, ehr_data.spo2),
            'respiratory_rate': self.compare_values(device_data.resp_rate, ehr_data.resp_rate)
        }
        
        # Clinical accuracy thresholds
        thresholds = {
            'heart_rate': 2,  # ±2 BPM
            'systolic_bp': 5,  # ±5 mmHg
            'diastolic_bp': 5,  # ±5 mmHg
            'spo2': 1,  # ±1%
            'respiratory_rate': 2  # ±2 breaths/min
        }
        
        for metric, result in validation_results.items():
            assert result <= thresholds[metric], \
                f"{metric} accuracy exceeded threshold: {result} > {thresholds[metric]}"
        
        return True
    
    def test_infusion_pump_safety(self, pump_interface, medication_order):
        """Test infusion pump safety features and programming"""
        
        # Validate pump programming from EHR order
        programmed_params = pump_interface.program_infusion(medication_order)
        
        # Check hard limits
        assert programmed_params.rate <= medication_order.max_rate, \
            "Infusion rate exceeds maximum safe limit"
        
        # Validate drug library integration
        drug_library_check = pump_interface.validate_against_drug_library(medication_order)
        assert drug_library_check['approved'], \
            f"Drug library rejection: {drug_library_check['reason']}"
        
        # Test safety alerts
        test_overdose = medication_order.copy()
        test_overdose.rate = medication_order.max_rate * 2
        
        safety_response = pump_interface.program_infusion(test_overdose)
        assert safety_response['alert_triggered'], \
            "Safety alert not triggered for overdose scenario"
        
        return True
```

```python
class ClinicalAIModelValidator:
    def validate_clinical_algorithm(self, model, test_cases):
        """Validate clinical AI model against gold standard"""
        
        performance_metrics = {
            'sensitivity': 0,
            'specificity': 0,
            'ppv': 0,  # Positive Predictive Value
            'npv': 0,  # Negative Predictive Value
            'auc_roc': 0
        }
        
        for test_case in test_cases:

            "Sensitivity below clinical acceptable threshold"
        assert performance_metrics['specificity'] >= 0.90, \
            "Specificity below clinical acceptable threshold"
        assert performance_metrics['auc_roc'] >= 0.85, \
            "Model discrimination insufficient for clinical use"
        
        return performance_metrics
    
    def test_sepsis_prediction_model(self):
        """Test sepsis prediction algorithm"""
```

- **Access Network**: 5G NR, LTE, Fiber, DSL, Cable
- **Core Network**: IMS, EPC, 5GC for packet switching and session management
- **Transport Network**: IP/MPLS, DWDM, Microwave for backhaul
- **Service Platforms**: VoLTE, IoT, Cloud Communications, Enterprise Services

**Key Network Elements:**
- **eNodeB/gNodeB**: Radio access network elements for 4G/5G
- **MME/AMF**: Mobility management entities
- **SGW/PGW/UPF**: Data plane gateways and user plane functions
- **HSS/UDM**: Subscriber data management
- **PCRF/PCF**: Policy and charging control
- **CSCF**: Call session control for IMS

**Service Delivery Architecture:**
- **BSS (Business Support Systems)**: CRM, billing, order management
- **OSS (Operations Support Systems)**: Network management, provisioning, fault management
- **Service Delivery Platforms**: Value-added services, APIs
- **Mediation Systems**: CDR processing and normalization

**Protocols & Interfaces:**
- **Radio Protocols**: NR, LTE, 3GPP standards
- **Core Protocols**: GTP, Diameter, SIP, HTTP/2
- **Management Protocols**: SNMP, NETCONF, RESTCONF
- **Billing Protocols**: ASN.1, TAP3, NRTRDE

Feature: 5G Network Service Validation

    When either party ends the call
    Then call teardown should complete successfully

  Scenario: 5G to 4G handover during active data session

    And no data should be lost during handover
    And charging should continue without interruption

```yaml
    - transport_slicing:
        focus: ["network_virtualization", "qos_enforcement"]
    - core_slicing:
        focus: ["network_function_selection", "policy_enforcement"]
```

**Slice Isolation Testing:**
```python
class NetworkSliceValidator:
    def validate_slice_isolation(self, slice_a, slice_b):
        """Validate complete isolation between network slices"""
        
        # Test resource isolation in RAN
        ran_isolation = self.test_ran_resource_isolation(slice_a, slice_b)
        assert ran_isolation, "RAN resource isolation failed"
        
        # Test transport isolation
        transport_isolation = self.test_transport_isolation(slice_a, slice_b)
        assert transport_isolation, "Transport isolation failed"
        
        # Test core network isolation
        core_isolation = self.test_core_isolation(slice_a, slice_b)
        assert core_isolation, "Core network isolation failed"
        
        # Test performance isolation
        performance_isolation = self.test_performance_isolation(slice_a, slice_b)
        assert performance_isolation, "Performance isolation failed"
        
        return True
    
    def test_slice_performance_guarantees(self, slice_config, traffic_profile):
        """Validate slice meets performance guarantees"""
        
        performance_metrics = {
            'throughput': self.measure_throughput(slice_config, traffic_profile),
            'latency': self.measure_latency(slice_config, traffic_profile),
            'reliability': self.measure_reliability(slice_config, traffic_profile),
            'availability': self.measure_availability(slice_config)
        }
        
        # Validate against slice SLA
        sla_requirements = slice_config['sla_requirements']
        
        assert performance_metrics['throughput'] >= sla_requirements['min_throughput'], \
            "Throughput SLA not met"
        assert performance_metrics['latency'] <= sla_requirements['max_latency'], \
            "Latency SLA not met"
        assert performance_metrics['reliability'] >= sla_requirements['min_reliability'], \
            "Reliability SLA not met"
        assert performance_metrics['availability'] >= sla_requirements['min_availability'], \
            "Availability SLA not met"
        
        return performance_metrics
```

- **Slice instantiation and activation**: Complete lifecycle management
- **Dynamic slice modification**: On-the-fly parameter changes
- **Cross-slice interference**: Resource contention scenarios
- **Slice admission control**: Resource allocation policies

**Multi-Domain Coordination Testing:**

questions.question: What's the comprehensive approach for testing billing system accuracy in complex telecom environments?
questions.answer:
**Telecom Billing System Testing Strategy:**

**End-to-End Billing Flow Testing:**

**CDR Generation & Collection Testing:**
```python
class BillingSystemValidator:
    def validate_cdr_generation(self, service_usage, expected_cdr_fields):
        """Validate CDR generation for various service types"""
        
        service_cdrs = {
            'voice': self.generate_voice_cdr(service_usage),
            'data': self.generate_data_cdr(service_usage),
            'sms': self.generate_sms_cdr(service_usage),
            'mms': self.generate_mms_cdr(service_usage),
            'volte': self.generate_volte_cdr(service_usage)
        }
        
        for service_type, cdr in service_cdrs.items():
            # Validate mandatory fields
            for field in expected_cdr_fields[service_type]:
                assert field in cdr, f"Missing mandatory field {field} in {service_type} CDR"
            
            # Validate field formats and values
            self.validate_cdr_field_values(cdr, service_usage)
        
        return service_cdrs
    
    def test_rating_engine_accuracy(self, cdrs, tariff_plan):
        """Validate rating engine applies correct charges"""
        
        rated_cdrs = self.rating_engine.process_cdrs(cdrs, tariff_plan)
        
        expected_charges = self.calculate_expected_charges(cdrs, tariff_plan)
        
        for cdr in rated_cdrs:
            expected_charge = expected_charges[cdr['record_id']]
            
            # Allow small rounding differences
            charge_difference = abs(cdr['total_charge'] - expected_charge)
            assert charge_difference < 0.01, \
                f"Rating error for {cdr['record_id']}: {cdr['total_charge']} vs {expected_charge}"
            
            # Validate tax and fee calculations
            self.validate_tax_calculations(cdr, tariff_plan)
        
        return rated_cdrs
```

**Revenue Assurance Testing:**

**CDR Reconciliation Process:**
```sql
-- SQL queries for revenue assurance validation
-- Check for missing CDRs
SELECT network_element, service_type, COUNT(*) as missing_cdrs
FROM expected_usage eu
LEFT JOIN actual_cdrs ac ON eu.usage_id = ac.correlation_id
WHERE ac.correlation_id IS NULL
GROUP BY network_element, service_type;

-- Check for CDR duplicates
SELECT correlation_id, COUNT(*) as duplicate_count
FROM actual_cdrs
GROUP BY correlation_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

-- Validate CDR sequence integrity
SELECT network_element, MAX(cdr_sequence) as max_sequence, COUNT(*) as total_cdrs
FROM actual_cdrs
GROUP BY network_element
HAVING MAX(cdr_sequence) != COUNT(*);
```
